'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**Seven teenagers are killed and two others injured after government forces airstrike a village in [[Savanes Region, Togo|Savanes Region]], [[Togo]]. Togolese authorities say that they mistook the teenagers for [[jihadists]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/togos-army-says-civilians-were-killed-by-airstrike-mistaken-jihadists-2022-07-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Pakistan floods]]; [[2022 Quetta floods]]
**At least 57 people are killed by floods in [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]] (mostly in [[Quetta]]) and two others are killed in [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/7/9/flooding-in-pakistan-kills-dozens-amid-heavy-monsoon-rains (Al Jazeera)]
*At least 13 people are killed and eight others injured when a minivan crashes into a tree in [[Polotitlán de la Ilustración]], [[State of Mexico]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2022/06/18/choque-de-una-combi-contra-un-arbol-en-la-mexico-queretaro-dejo-12-muertos/ (Infobae)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Guatemala]]
***[[Guatemala]] puts 66 of [[Municipalities of Guatemala|its municipalities]] on alert due to a sharp increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2022/07/09/guatemala-aumenta-a-66-sus-municipios-en-alerta-roja-por-la-covid-19/ (Infobae)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Four people are wounded in a [[mass stabbing]] at a hospital in [[Shanghai]], [[China]]. Police open fire and subdue the assailant. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/4-stabbed-at-shanghai-hospital-after-crowd-held-hostage-police-open-fire-3142126 (NDTV)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2019–present Sri Lankan economic crisis]], [[2022 Sri Lankan protests]]
**[[President of Sri Lanka|President]] [[Gotabaya Rajapaksa]] flees his residence in [[Colombo]] after protesters storm the residence and clash with police. At least 33 people are injured. Rajapaksa's resignation is demanded amid the worst [[economy of Sri Lanka|economic]] crisis in [[Sri Lanka]] since 1948. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-62104268 (BBC News)]
**The office of the [[Prime Minister of Sri Lanka|Prime Minister]] announces that [[Ranil Wickremesinghe]] has agreed to resign after party leaders in Parliament call for his resignation. [https://www.irishtimes.com/world/asia-pacific/2022/07/09/sri-lankan-prime-minister-willing-to-resign-make-way-for-new-government-amid-protests/ (''The Irish Times'')]
**Wickremesinghe's private residence is [[arson|set on fire]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/protesters-set-sri-lankan-pm-ranil-wickremesinghe-s-residence-on-fire-101657381849320.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
**[[Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka|Speaker of the Parliament]] [[Mahinda Yapa Abeywardena]] says that Rajapaksa has agreed to resign on July 13. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/sri-lanka-s-president-to-resign-on-july-13-pm-s-house-attacked-top-facts-101657384355390-amp.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*[[Government of Ukraine]]
** [[President of Ukraine|President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] dismisses Ukraine's ambassadors to Germany, India, the Czech Republic, Norway and Hungary. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/volodymyr-zelensky-ukraine-ambassadors-sacked-b2119750.html (''Independent'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 Wimbledon Championships]]
**In tennis, [[Elena Rybakina]] of [[Kazakhstan]] wins her first [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] title after defeating [[Ons Jabeur]] of [[Tunisia]] in the [[2022 Wimbledon Championships – Women's singles|women's singles]] final, 3–6, 6–2, 6–2. Rybakina becomes the first Kazakh player to win a Grand Slam singles title. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/07/09/wimbledon-ladies-final/ (''The Washington Post'')]
